info.name: Unitill API
info.description:
Complete API collection for the Unitill backend (Laravel).

## Setup
1. Set the `base_url` collection variable (e.g. `http://localhost/unitill-backend/public/api`).
2. Call **Auth → Login** (or **Verify Student Email**) and copy the returned `token` into the `token` variable.
3. For dashboard endpoints, call **Admin · Auth → Admin Login** and copy the token into `admin_token`.

## Response envelope
- Success: `{ "status": true, "data": ..., "message": ... }`
- Error: `{ "status": false, "message": ..., "data": ... }`

Send the `lang` header (`en`/`ar`) to control the language of returned messages.

item.name: Auth · V2 (OTP login)

exec: // Carry the user_id straight into the verify-otp step.

request.description:
Step 1 of 2. Verifies the password and emails a 6-digit code. Returns **no tokens**.

Required: `type`, `password`, `device_id` (or `device_identifier`), and one of `email` / `login` (`login` accepts email or phone).

Optional: `device_type` (ios|android), `device_token`, `device_name`, `city_name`, `country_code` (2 letters), `enable_biometric`.

response.name: Login — OTP sent

originalRequest.description:
Step 1 of 2. Verifies the password and emails a 6-digit code. Returns **no tokens**.

Required: `type`, `password`, `device_id` (or `device_identifier`), and one of `email` / `login` (`login` accepts email or phone).

Optional: `device_type` (ios|android), `device_token`, `device_name`, `city_name`, `country_code` (2 letters), `enable_biometric`.

request.description:
Same step 1, but authenticates with a stored biometric token instead of a password.

Required: `type` = `fingerprint`, `biometric_token` (min 20 chars), `device_id`. The device must already be registered for that user.

Note: v2 still sends an OTP after a successful fingerprint check — biometrics replace the password, not the second factor.

response.name: Fingerprint Login — OTP sent

originalRequest.description:
Same step 1, but authenticates with a stored biometric token instead of a password.

Required: `type` = `fingerprint`, `biometric_token` (min 20 chars), `device_id`. The device must already be registered for that user.

Note: v2 still sends an OTP after a successful fingerprint check — biometrics replace the password, not the second factor.

exec: // Store the tokens so the rest of the collection can use them.

request.description:
Step 2 of 2. Verifies the code and issues the tokens. The OTP is consumed, so it cannot be replayed.

Required: `otp` (exactly 6 digits) plus one identifier — `user_id`, `student_email`, or `email`.

### ⚠️ Always send device_id here
The API marks it *optional*, but this is the request that creates the refresh token. Omit it and it is stored as an empty string, and every later `auth/refresh` fails with `refresh_token_invalid` — even though refresh *requires* `device_id`. Send the same value you will use at refresh.

Optional: `device_type`, `device_token`, `device_name`, `city_name`, `country_code`, `enable_biometric` (set true to also receive a `biometric_token` for fingerprint login).

Optional: `device_type`, `device_token`, `device_name`, `city_name`, `country_code`, `enable_biometric` (set true to also receive a `biometric_token` for fingerprint login).

request.description:
Re-sends the code for a login already in progress. Send one identifier — `user_id`, `student_email`, or `email`.

Only works while a challenge is pending: if no OTP is outstanding it returns 400. Rate limited to one send per 60s (`mobile_auth.login_otp_resend_cooldown`); too soon returns 429 with `retry_after_seconds`.

exec: // Rotation: the old refresh token is now dead — store the new one.

request.description:
Exchanges a refresh token for a new 30-day access token.

Required: `refresh_token` (min 20 chars) and `device_id` (or `device_identifier`).

**Rotation:** each call revokes the token you sent and returns a new one — a refresh token is single-use. Reusing an old one returns `refresh_token_revoked`.

`error_code` in the error body tells you which check failed:
- `refresh_token_invalid` — no row matched. The `device_id` differs from the one sent to verify-otp, or the token is wrong.
- `refresh_token_revoked` — already used, or logged out.
- `refresh_token_expired` — older than 30 days; log in again.

item.description:
Two-step login. Step 1 (`login`) only emails a one-time code — **no tokens are returned**. Step 2 (`login/verify-otp`) verifies the code and issues the tokens. The access token lives 30 days (v1: 60 min).

### ⚠️ device_id must be identical in every call
The refresh token is stored against the `device_id` sent to **verify-otp**, and `auth/refresh` looks the token up by `token_hash` + `device_id`. If they differ you get `refresh_token_invalid`.

Because v2 splits login into two requests, the `device_id` you send to **login** is *never persisted* — only the one sent to **verify-otp** counts. Every request here uses the `{{device_id}}` collection variable so they can't drift apart. Set it once in the collection variables.

Enters the same publication flow as POST /ads: free quota -> coupon -> Stripe. When payment is due the response carries payment_intent_id and client_secret; the ad stays "draft" until Stripe confirms via webhook.
Fallback verification after the mobile/web Stripe SDK confirms the PaymentIntent. The signed Stripe webhook publishes automatically, so normally this request is not needed.

header.value: Use a signature generated by Stripe or Stripe CLI
header.description: Required. This endpoint rejects unsigned requests.

request.description: Stripe calls this after payment_intent.succeeded and the ad is published immediately. Test with: stripe listen --forward-to {{base_url}}/stripe/webhook

Step 4 (Pay) of the Sell flow: previews a discount code against the
current listing fee. Does NOT consume the code — that happens when the
ad is actually published, by sending `coupon_code` to POST /ads.

Success returns discount_amount, final_amount and formatted variants.

Failures return 422 with data.code set to one of:
  invalid        — no such code, or the code is switched off
  not_started    — the code has a future start date
  expired        — past its expiry date
  exhausted      — the overall usage limit is reached
  already_used   — THIS user already redeemed it (one use per user)
  min_amount     — the fee is below the code's minimum spend

Codes are matched case-insensitively.

item.description:
Sorting and filtering on GET /ads.

Every response carries `sort_options` (localised, includes the Cars-only mileage/year entries when the category defines those attributes), `current_sort`, `applied_filters`, `active_filter_count`, and `filter_options` for the resolved category.

Attribute filters are any query key that is not a reserved one; `lat`, `lng`, `postcode` and `radius_km` are reserved and are never treated as attributes.

item.description: One request per category, attributes matching CategoryAttributeSeeder. Electronics subcategories (Laptops, Mobile phones, Tablets, Computers, Home Electronics) carry their own attribute sets; Accessories/Others inherit the Electronics set.

item.name: Lookups

query.description: Required. UK format, space optional (LS29JT works too).

request.description:
Resolves a UK postcode via postcodes.io.

Returns: postcode, region, latitude, longitude, city, city_id.

`city_id` is matched against the local cities table by name and is
null when there is no match — the client must then let the user pick
a city manually, since city_id is REQUIRED when creating an ad.

Errors: 422 on a malformed postcode, 404 when postcodes.io has no
match or is unreachable.

query.description: Required. Format AB12CDE — 2 letters, 2 digits, 3 letters, no space.

request.description:
Looks up a UK registration and returns vehicle details for the Cars
Post-Ad step. Results are cached for 24h.

The query param is `plate` (not `license_plate` — that is the field
name used when creating the ad).

Maps to: make, model, year, fuel_type, transmission, body_type, colour.
It does NOT return mileage, engine_size or seats — the user enters those.

All returned values are editable by the user before posting.

Errors: 422 on a malformed plate, 404 when the vehicle is not found.
Requires services.vehicle_api.key to be configured.

item.description:
Helper lookups used while filling in the Sell (Post New Ad) form.
Both require a logged-in user (they sit behind auth:sanctum).

Postcode -> city/area feeds the Location step for every category.
Vehicle plate -> Make/Model/Year/Fuel pre-fills the Cars step (editable).

item.name: My Ads

formdata.description: Optional. Applied to the listing fee; single use per user.

request.description:
Reactivates a paused or expired ad for a new 30-day period.

CHARGED like a new listing: any previous Stripe intent is cleared and the ad re-enters the fee path (free quota -> coupon -> Stripe). The ad becomes "pending" and only goes live once payment settles.

formdata.description: Optional. Applied to the listing fee; single use per user.

variable.description: Id or public_id of a SOLD ad

request.description:
Copies a sold ad into a brand new listing. Only status "sold" is accepted (422 otherwise) — use Activate Ad for paused/expired.

The copy gets a new id and public_id, carries over the images, attributes, price and location, and starts with a clean sale/payment record. The original stays "sold" so the purchase history and its archived chats are preserved.

A relist is a fresh 30-day listing, so it goes through the normal fee path: free quota -> coupon -> Stripe. Response includes publication.client_secret when payment is due; the new ad stays "pending" until the webhook confirms.

request.description:
Privacy & notification toggles for the Settings screen. Returned only to the account owner.

notify_system is always true — system alerts cannot be switched off.

Partial update — send only the toggles being changed.

Accepted: show_last_name, show_approximate_location, trusted_users_only, notify_chat, notify_ads.

NOT accepted: notify_system (always on; sending it alone returns 422).

Effects:
- show_last_name=false -> others see first name only, on the profile and on the seller block of your listings.
- trusted_users_only=true -> only fully verified accounts (status 1) can open a NEW chat with you; existing threads are unaffected. Blocked buyers get 403 with needs_verification.
- show_approximate_location -> stored, not yet enforced.

header.description: Set to "ar", "fr", "es" or "zh" for a translated message

request.description:
GDPR Subject Access Request. Emails the full export to the account email as a JSON attachment (unitill-personal-data.json).

The payload covers all six items the spec requires: the copy of the data itself plus purposes_of_processing, categories_of_data, recipients, retention_periods and your_rights.

Responses:
- 200 confirmation that the email was sent
- 500 if delivery failed (no longer reported as success — a SAR has a statutory deadline)
- 429 when the export limit is exceeded (5 per hour per user; Retry-After and X-RateLimit-* headers included)

response.name: Request Data Export (GDPR) — Example

header.description: Affects error messages only; the export itself is English

request.description:
"Download my data" — the same payload as the SAR email, streamed inline as a JSON file so the app does not have to wait on mail delivery.

Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=unitill-personal-data-YYYY-MM-DD.json

Includes 15 data sections: ads, favourites, conversations, messages sent, ad reports, chat reports, ratings given/received, orders as buyer/seller, coupon redemptions, devices, login history, notifications, contact-us messages.

Throttled to 5 requests per hour per user (shared with the SAR endpoint) because each call reads 15 tables. Exceeding it returns 429 with Retry-After.

`type`: "user" reports the other participant, "chat" reports the conversation.
`reason` must be a value from GET /chat-report-reasons (free text is rejected).
